title: CORNER Product Website: The Heaven Spec
summary: Full design and content spec for corner.app, the Corner product website. 'Landed in heaven' design language. Ultra clean, white, spacious, calm. Every page spec'd with layout, copy, visual direction, and responsive behavior. The site that sells the operating system.
content:
CORNER Product Website: The Heaven Spec

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Steffen (visual design) + Bobby (implementation) Domain: corner.app (or corneros.com, usecorner.com as alternatives) Purpose: Sell Corner. Convert visitors into trial signups. Establish Corner as a serious platform, not a toy.

Design Language: "Landed in Heaven"

Patrik's directive: the site should feel like you landed in heaven.

Not metaphorical. Literal design intent. When someone opens corner.app, the feeling should be relief. Calm. Spaciousness. Like walking into a perfectly clean, white room with natural light pouring in. No visual clutter. No dark theme. No tech-bro energy. No startup noise.

The feeling: You just stepped out of the chaos of running a business and into the place where everything is handled.

Design Principles

  1. White is the canvas. Background is white (#FFFFFF) or near-white (#FAFAFA). Not gray. Not cream. Pure, clean white. Content floats on it.

  2. Space is a feature. Generous padding everywhere. Sections breathe. Nothing touches anything else. If it feels empty, it's working. The emptiness is the point. It communicates: "We have room for you."

  3. Type does the work. No decorative elements. No gradients. No patterns. No textures. The typography carries every section. Beautiful, confident, large type on white space.

  4. One accent color. A single, warm accent. Not aggressive. Think: soft amber (#E8A845), warm sage (#7C9A72), or a muted coral. Steffen calls it. Used sparingly: CTAs, the occasional highlight, interactive states. The site is 95% black-on-white with 5% accent.

  5. Isometric art is the soul. The isometric game art appears throughout, but gently. Not overwhelming. Small illustrations floating in the white space. A little office scene here. An agent character there. The art humanizes the white space without cluttering it.

  6. Motion is slow. No fast animations. Everything eases in slowly. Fade-ups at 600-800ms. Parallax at 0.3x speed. Elements appear like they're waking up, not jumping out. The site breathes.

  7. Photography is human. Where photos appear (team, testimonials), they're warm. Natural light. Candid, not posed. Real people in real offices. Not stock photos. Never stock photos.

How This Differs from aheadofmarket.com

aheadofmarket.com is AOM's site. Dark, cinematic, bold orange, high-energy. That's the production company.

corner.app is the product site. White, calm, spacious, gentle warmth. That's the AI operations platform.

They share DNA (the same team built both), but Corner's site reflects the product experience: stepping into your own world where everything is handled.

Site Architecture

corner.app/
  /                   Homepage (the pitch)
  /product            Product deep-dive (the how)
  /pricing            Pricing page (already spec'd)
  /demo               Interactive demo (the proof)
  /customers          Case studies + testimonials
  /construction       Industry: Corner for Construction
  /cpa                Industry: Corner for CPAs
  /law                Industry: Corner for Law
  /developers         SDK + API docs
  /academy            Corner Academy (learning platform)
  /blog               Blog / updates
  /about              About AOM + Corner
  /book               Book a demo / contact
  /login              Dashboard login
  /signup             Onboarding wizard
  /careers            Hiring page

Page 1: Homepage (corner.app/)

The homepage is the pitch. 7 sections. One scrolling narrative. Each section earns the next scroll.

Section 1: Hero

Layout: Full viewport. Center-aligned content. White background. Isometric office illustration floating subtly below the text (40% opacity, parallax on scroll).

Headline:

Your AI team is already working.

Large. 56-72px on desktop. Weight 600. Letter-spacing: -0.03em. The headline should feel like a statement of fact, not a sales pitch.

Subheadline:

Corner gives you a team of AI agents that manage your operations,
organize your work, and keep your business moving. Every day.
Without you lifting a finger.

16-20px. Weight 400. Max-width: 640px. Color: #555 (softer than the headline).

CTA:

[Start Free Trial]    [Watch Demo]

Primary CTA: filled button, accent color. Secondary: text button, underline on hover.

Below the fold indicator: Subtle down arrow or "scroll" text. Barely visible. Just enough to invite the next section.

What's NOT here: No navigation bar initially. The nav fades in after scrolling past the hero. The hero is a moment. Let it breathe.

Section 2: The Isometric Office (Product Preview)

Layout: Full-width. White background with a very subtle warm tint (#FDFCFA). The isometric office takes center stage.

Content: A static but beautiful render of a Corner office. 4-5 agents visible, each in a different state (one working, one chatting, one walking, one idle). Speech bubbles showing real-looking agent output. The office is furnished, warm, alive.

Caption below the image:

This is your office. These are your agents.
They're working right now.

14-16px. Centered. Understated.

Interaction: On hover/tap, each agent shows a tooltip with their name and role. "Bobby - Web Developer." "Operations - Your Chief of Staff." Not clickable (that's the demo page). Just a taste.

Section 3: Three Modes

Layout: Three columns (desktop). Stacked (mobile). Each column shows one mode.

Left: The Game

  • Small isometric illustration (zoomed-in view of one room)
  • Title: "The Game"
  • Description: "Your AI team as an isometric office. Watch agents work in real-time. Click to chat. Drag to organize. The most satisfying way to manage a business."

Center: The Checklist

  • Small illustration of a clean, minimal task list
  • Title: "The Checklist"
  • Description: "Simple. Drag tasks. Check them off. See what every agent is working on right now. For when you need to move fast."

Right: The Megaboard

  • Small illustration of charts and stats
  • Title: "The Megaboard"
  • Description: "Everything at a glance. Hours saved, tasks completed, agent performance, ROI. The stats that prove it's working."

Below the three columns:

Three ways to see the same system. Live where you want.

Section 4: How It Works (3 Steps)

Layout: Horizontal flow with connecting line (desktop). Vertical steps (mobile). Large numbers (1, 2, 3) as design elements.

Step 1: Tell us about your business. "Answer a few questions. Our onboarding wizard learns your industry, team size, and biggest pain points. Two minutes."

Step 2: Meet your team. "We assemble your AI team based on what you told us. Operations. Calendar. Email. Outreach. Content. Each agent is specialized and ready."

Step 3: Watch them work. "Open your office. Your agents are already moving. Tasks being organized. Emails being triaged. Calendar being optimized. You didn't do anything. They did."

Subtext:

No setup guide. No onboarding video.
Your team figures it out.

Section 5: Who It's For

Layout: Horizontal cards. Each card is an industry/persona. Soft illustration per card.

Card 1: Contractors "Scheduling, estimating, permits, client communication. Your agents handle the office while you're on the job site."

Card 2: CPAs "Document collection, deadline tracking, client reminders, tax prep organization. Tax season doesn't have to be chaos."

Card 3: Law Firms "Case research, client intake, deadline management, document drafting. Your paralegal agent never sleeps."

Card 4: Any Small Business "If you run a business and wish you had a back office, Corner is your back office."

Subtext:

Built for businesses that are too busy to manage AI. And too smart to ignore it.

Section 6: Social Proof

Layout: Full-width. Subtle background shift (#F8F8F8). Testimonial cards.

If we have real testimonials (from AOM/Patrik's experience):

  • 2-3 quote cards with name, photo, business name
  • The quote should reference a specific outcome: "My email response time went from 2 hours to 15 minutes."

If we don't have testimonials yet (launch mode):

  • Stats from AOM's own usage: "14 agents. 500+ tasks completed. 200+ hours saved. One business."
  • Text: "AOM built Corner for themselves first. This is what it looks like when the product works."

Section 7: Bottom CTA

Layout: Full viewport. White background. Centered content. Large.

Headline:

Start for free. Stay because it works.

40-48px. Weight 600.

Subheadline:

7-day free trial. Full access. No restrictions.
Your AI team is 2 minutes away.

CTA:

[Start Your Free Trial]

Large button. Accent color. Centered.

Below the CTA:

Or book a 15-minute demo →

Text link.

Page 2: Product (corner.app/product)

The deep-dive. For the prospect who wants to understand HOW it works before committing.

Structure

  1. Hero: "This is what an AI team looks like." Full-width product screenshot or render.
  2. Agent Roster: Every agent type with name, icon, and 2-sentence description. Grid layout.
  3. Real-Time Demo Loop: Embedded video or animated GIF showing agent activity in real-time.
  4. Skills System: "Your agents learn new skills." Explanation of the skills architecture with examples.
  5. Security: "Your data is yours." Isolation, encryption, privacy explainer.
  6. Architecture: "How it runs." Technical overview for the buyer who needs to understand the stack. CC, Docker, Supabase, WebSocket. Simplified.
  7. Integrations: Logo grid of tools Corner connects to (QuickBooks, Salesforce, Slack, Gmail, Zapier, etc.).
  8. CTA: "Start Free Trial."

Visual Treatment

Every section alternates between white (#FFFFFF) and near-white (#FAFAFA) backgrounds. Content max-width: 1120px. Images bleed wider (1280px or full-width where appropriate).

Isometric illustrations scattered throughout. Not as decoration. As explanation. "Here's what happens when your email agent triages your inbox" with a small scene showing an agent at a desk, envelopes floating in, sorted piles going out.

Page 3: Demo (corner.app/demo)

Concept

An interactive, sandboxed Corner office. Visitor explores without signing up. Pre-populated with sample data: a fictional business called "Phoenix Plumbing" with 4 agents working.

What the Demo Shows

  • Isometric office with agents moving and working
  • Chat with a demo agent (pre-scripted responses, not live CC)
  • Switch between Game, Checklist, and Megaboard modes
  • See sample tasks, sample agent outputs, sample ROI report
  • Explore the room (click agents, open task HUD, browse checklist)

Constraints

  • No real AI. Demo agents respond with pre-written scripts.
  • No account creation required. Fully anonymous.
  • Session expires after 15 minutes. "Want to keep going? Start your free trial."
  • Data resets on every visit. No persistence.

Why a Demo Page

The audit onboarding at /audit/test proves the pattern: let people interact before asking them to commit. The Corner demo does the same thing. "Don't trust what we say. Try it."

Page 4: Customers (corner.app/customers)

Structure

  1. Hero: "Businesses running on Corner." Subtitle: "Real businesses. Real results."
  2. Case Study Cards: Grid of 3-6 case studies. Each card: business logo, industry tag, headline metric ("47 hours saved per month"), 1-sentence quote.
  3. Full Case Study Page (per customer): Company background, problem, solution (which agents, which skills), results (metrics), quote, before/after comparison.
  4. Industry Filter: Construction / CPA / Law / Other. Filter the grid.
  5. CTA: "Start your own story."

Early Stage Strategy

Until real customers exist, this page features:

  • AOM as Case Study #1 (the proof of concept)
  • Any beta users from the initial launch
  • Placeholder for future case studies: "Your story here. Start your free trial."

Page 5: Industry Pages (corner.app/construction, /cpa, /law)

Each industry page follows the same template but with industry-specific content.

Template Structure

  1. Hero: Industry-specific headline. Isometric illustration with industry theme (hard hats for construction, calculators for CPA, gavels for law).
  2. Pain Points: 3-4 specific problems this industry faces that Corner solves.
  3. Agent Roster: The agents pre-configured for this industry. Names, descriptions, example outputs.
  4. Sample Day: "What a day looks like with Corner." 6AM-6PM timeline showing agent activity.
  5. ROI Calculator: Industry-specific inputs and outputs. "Enter your number of monthly invoices. Here's how many hours Corner saves you."
  6. Testimonial: Industry-specific quote (or AOM-as-proxy).
  7. CTA: "Start your [Industry] Corner."

Industry-Specific Content

Construction (corner.app/construction):

  • Headline: "Your office runs itself. You run the job site."
  • Pain points: scheduling chaos, missed permits, estimating bottlenecks, client communication gaps
  • Agents: Estimating, Dispatch, Permits, Safety, Client Comms, Invoicing
  • Room theme preview: hard hats, blueprints, tool walls

CPA (corner.app/cpa):

  • Headline: "Tax season without the chaos."
  • Pain points: document collection delays, missed deadlines, manual client reminders, prep bottlenecks
  • Agents: Tax Prep, Document Collection, Deadline Tracking, Client Communication, Review, Biz Dev
  • Room theme preview: mahogany desk, filing cabinets, calculator

Law (corner.app/law):

  • Headline: "Your agents never forget a deadline."
  • Pain points: calendar/deadline complexity, client intake volume, research time, billing inefficiency
  • Agents: Case Research, Client Intake, Deadline/Calendar, Document Drafting, Billing, Discovery
  • Room theme preview: law library, bookshelves, gavel

Page 6: Developers (corner.app/developers)

Structure

  1. Hero: "Build on Corner." Code snippet showing the SDK in action. Dark code block on white background (the only dark element on the site).
  2. SDK Overview: JavaScript SDK, REST API, WebSocket API, Webhooks. 4 cards with brief descriptions.
  3. Interactive API Playground: Try an API call in the browser. Pre-authenticated sandbox.
  4. Documentation Link: "Read the Docs" button linking to full API documentation.
  5. Developer Program: Sign up, build skills, sell on the marketplace. Revenue share info.
  6. Open-Source: Link to corner-engine GitHub (when available).
  7. CTA: "Get your API key."

Visual Treatment

The developer page can have more technical energy than the rest of the site. Code snippets with syntax highlighting. Terminal-style fonts for API examples. But still on the white canvas. The code blocks are islands of dark in a sea of white.

Page 7: Academy (corner.app/academy)

Structure

  1. Hero: "Learn AI operations." Subtitle: "Courses built from real business experience. Not theory."
  2. Course Grid: Card grid of available courses. Each card: thumbnail, title, duration, difficulty badge, lesson count.
  3. Featured Course: Full-width highlight of the flagship course ("AI Operations for Small Business").
  4. For Businesses: "Courses tailored to your Corner data. Your agents, your tasks, your numbers."
  5. For Educators: "Bring Corner to your classroom." University/bootcamp partnership info.
  6. CTA: "Start learning" (for subscribers) or "Start free trial to access Academy" (for visitors).

Page 8: About (corner.app/about)

Structure

  1. Hero: "Built by people who run a business." No corporate speak. Real story.
  2. The Story: How AOM built the system for themselves, realized it was sellable, and turned it into Corner. Honest. No mythologizing.
  3. The Team: Patrik, Ash. Real photos. Brief bios. Human.
  4. The Agents: The AI team, presented like real team members. Bobby, Operations, Calendar, etc. Isometric portraits. "They're not human. But they work like they are."
  5. Values: 3-4 core beliefs. Brief.
    • "AI should do the work, not make more work."
    • "Your data is yours. Period."
    • "Simple enough for your mom. Powerful enough for your CTO."
    • "Built for the businesses that big tech forgot."
  6. CTA: "Join us" (link to careers) or "Try Corner" (link to signup).

Page 9: Blog (corner.app/blog)

Structure

Standard blog layout. Card grid with featured post. Categories: Product Updates, AI Operations, Industry Insights, Engineering.

Visual Treatment

White background. Cards with subtle shadow. Large featured image per post. Clean typography. Generous line height (1.8) for body text. Max-width: 720px for article content.

Content Strategy

  • Weekly: Product updates, new features, skill releases
  • Bi-weekly: AI operations insights (from Steve's research, anonymized platform data)
  • Monthly: Industry deep-dives (construction AI, CPA AI, law AI)
  • Quarterly: Corner State of AI Operations report (platform intelligence, anonymized)

Page 10: Careers (corner.app/careers)

Structure

  1. Hero: "Build the future of work." Subtitle: "Corner is small. The mission is not."
  2. Open Roles: Card list with role title, team, location, and brief description.
  3. Culture: "We ship every day. We trust our agents. We trust our people." Brief, real.
  4. Benefits: Whatever AOM offers. Honest about being a startup.
  5. CTA: "Apply" (per role, links to email or application form).

Global Elements

Navigation Bar

Desktop:

[Corner Logo]     Product  Pricing  Demo  Customers  Developers  Academy     [Login]  [Start Free Trial]
  • Logo: Corner wordmark. Clean. Simple. Left-aligned.
  • Links: 14-16px. Weight 500. #333. Hover: accent color.
  • Login: text link.
  • Start Free Trial: filled button, accent color.
  • Background: transparent on hero, white (#FFFFFF) with bottom border (#F0F0F0) once scrolled.
  • Sticky on scroll.

Mobile:

[Corner Logo]     [Hamburger]

Hamburger opens a full-screen overlay. White background. Large links (20px). CTA at the bottom.

Footer

Layout: 4 columns (desktop). 2 columns (tablet). Stacked (mobile).

Columns:

  1. Product: Features, Pricing, Demo, Customers, Academy
  2. Developers: SDK, API Docs, Marketplace, Open Source, Status
  3. Company: About, Blog, Careers, Contact, Press
  4. Legal: Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Security, GDPR

Bottom bar: Copyright. Social links (LinkedIn, Twitter/X, GitHub). "Built in Phoenix, AZ."

404 Page

A little isometric scene: an agent standing in an empty room, looking confused. Speech bubble: "This room doesn't exist yet. But yours does."

CTA: "Go Home" + "Start Free Trial"

Technical Spec

Stack

  • Framework: Next.js 14+ (App Router)
  • Hosting: Vercel
  • CMS: MDX for blog posts, static for everything else (content changes are code changes, not CMS updates)
  • Analytics: PostHog (same as the product)
  • Forms: Formspree (consistent with existing AOM setup)
  • Fonts: System font stack with a beautiful display font for headlines (Steffen calls it: candidates include Instrument Serif, Fraunces, or a clean sans like Inter/Satoshi)

Performance Targets

  • Lighthouse: 95+ on all metrics
  • LCP: <2.5s on mobile
  • CLS: 0
  • FID: <100ms
  • First load: <1MB transferred
  • Page transitions: <200ms

SEO

  • Static pages (SSG) for all marketing pages
  • Dynamic pages only for blog posts (ISR, revalidate every hour)
  • Structured data: Organization, Product, FAQ, Article schemas
  • Sitemap auto-generated
  • robots.txt allowing all crawlers
  • Open Graph images per page (Steffen designs)
  • Twitter Card meta tags

Accessibility

  • WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on all pages
  • All images have alt text
  • All interactive elements keyboard-navigable
  • Skip-to-content link
  • Focus indicators visible
  • Color contrast AA on all text
  • Screen reader tested (VoiceOver, NVDA)

Responsive Breakpoints

Breakpoint Target
390px Small mobile (iPhone SE)
430px Standard mobile (iPhone 15)
768px Tablet (iPad)
1024px Small laptop
1280px Standard desktop
1440px Large desktop
1920px Ultra-wide

Content max-width: 1120px. Bleed sections: full-width or 1280px.

Content Guidelines

Voice

Corner's voice is different from AOM's. AOM is bold, high-energy, "we get it." Corner is calm, confident, quiet. "We handle it."

Corner tone:

  • Quiet confidence. Not loud. Not salesy.
  • Explanatory without being technical. A plumber reads this and understands.
  • Warm but professional. Not casual, not corporate.
  • Short sentences. Short paragraphs. Let the white space do work.
  • Never say "AI-powered." Everyone says that. Say what the AI actually does.

Words we use: agents, team, office, working, handled, organized, managed, clear, simple, yours Words we avoid: revolutionary, cutting-edge, leverage, synergy, disruptive, AI-powered, machine learning, neural network, transformative

Copy Length

  • Headlines: 3-8 words maximum
  • Subheadlines: 15-25 words maximum
  • Body paragraphs: 2-3 sentences maximum
  • Feature descriptions: 1-2 sentences
  • Page total word count: 300-600 words per page (excluding blog/docs)

The less text on the page, the more the design works.

Steffen's Design Deliverables

Priority 1 (Launch)

  1. Design system: Colors (accent color selection), typography (display font + body font), spacing scale, component library (buttons, cards, inputs, badges)
  2. Homepage design: All 7 sections. Desktop and mobile.
  3. Isometric art direction: How Corner's game art appears on the marketing site. Size, opacity, placement guidelines.
  4. Navigation + Footer: Desktop and mobile layouts.
  5. Agent character portraits: Marketing versions of the isometric agents for the product page and industry pages.
  6. CTA button design: Primary, secondary, ghost. Hover states. Mobile tap targets.

Priority 2 (Pre-Launch)

  1. Product page design
  2. Industry page template (one design, 3 content variants)
  3. Customer/case study page template
  4. Blog post template
  5. 404 page illustration
  6. OG images: Per-page social sharing cards (1200x630)

Priority 3 (Post-Launch)

  1. Demo page UX (interactive prototype)
  2. Developer page design (code snippet styling, API playground)
  3. Academy page design
  4. Careers page design

Bobby's Implementation Checklist

Phase 1: Launch (Ship These First)

  • Next.js project setup (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind)
  • Deploy to Vercel on corner.app (or temp domain until domain acquired)
  • Global layout: nav + footer + page transitions
  • Homepage: all 7 sections
  • Pricing page (already spec'd in pricing-page-spec.md)
  • Book/contact page (reuse existing /book pattern)
  • Login redirect (to dashboard when product is ready)
  • Signup redirect (to onboarding wizard when product is ready)
  • PostHog analytics integration
  • SEO: meta tags, OG images, structured data, sitemap
  • Responsive: all breakpoints tested

Phase 2: Pre-Launch

  • Product page
  • 3 industry pages (construction, CPA, law)
  • Customers page (AOM as case study #1)
  • About page
  • Blog (MDX setup + first 3 posts)
  • 404 page

Phase 3: Post-Launch

  • Interactive demo page
  • Developer page + API documentation
  • Academy page
  • Careers page
  • Blog RSS feed
  • Newsletter signup (integrate with email tool)

Competitive Website Analysis

Sites That Nail "Heaven" Energy

Linear.app: Ultra-clean. Dark theme, but the spacing and typography are heaven-tier. Study: their section transitions, their use of whitespace, their feature illustration style.

Notion.com: White, spacious, warm. The way they use illustration + type is closest to what Corner's homepage should feel like. Study: their homepage hero, their product screenshots, their footer design.

Vercel.com: Engineering beauty. The grid system, the card components, the code snippet styling. Study: their developer page, their pricing page, their changelog.

Arc.net: The purest "heaven" energy in tech. White, enormous type, barely any content per section. Study: their homepage. That's the energy level. Corner should feel this clean.

Framer.com: The animation quality. Smooth, slow, intentional. Study: their homepage scroll animations. That's the speed Corner should animate at.

What Corner Should NOT Look Like

  • HubSpot/Salesforce: Too corporate. Too busy. Too many CTAs competing for attention.
  • Most AI startups: Too dark. Too "tech." Purple gradients and particle effects. Corner is the anti-AI-startup.
  • Cheap SaaS sites: Template energy. Unsplash stock photos. Generic copy. Corner must feel custom-built, because it is.

Domain Strategy

Primary: corner.app (ideal, check availability)

Alternatives:

  • usecorner.com
  • corneros.com (Corner OS)
  • getcorner.com
  • cornerhq.com
  • corner.so

Requirements:

  • .app or .com TLD (credibility)
  • Short, memorable, typeable
  • No hyphens
  • Available on all major social platforms (@corner or @corneros)

Launch Sequence

  1. Now: Steve specs (this document). Steffen designs. Bobby scaffolds.
  2. C3 build: Homepage + pricing + book page go live. "Coming Soon" energy with an email capture.
  3. C4 launch: Full site live. Signup works. Demo page works. Product page reflects real features.
  4. C5+: Industry pages, developer page, academy page added as features ship.

The site grows with the product. Don't build pages for features that don't exist yet. But always have the next page ready to ship the day the feature launches.

The Corner website is the first impression. It should feel like the product: calm, organized, handled. The visitor arrives stressed (they're a business owner, of course they're stressed). They leave feeling like someone just offered to carry half the weight. That's the conversion. Not a button click. A feeling.

"You just walked into the quietest, cleanest room you've ever seen. And there's a team in here, already working. For you."
